# Wiki Log

Append-only chronological record of all wiki operations. Each entry starts with a consistent prefix for grep-parseability. When this file grows past 40 kB, `python -I scripts/rotate_log.py --write` moves the oldest entries to archive files of at most 40 kB each (`scripts/check.py` warns when it is time).

Older entries are in these archive files, oldest first:

## [2026-11-22] draft | Figure 1: the Fetterman label made wrappable; the whole-sentence rule written down

The rendered Figure 1 showed "Functional/metabolic/transcriptional" running out of its box: joined by slashes, the three words are one token that Mermaid cannot wrap. The label now reads "Functional, metabolic and transcriptional maturation largely independent (Fetterman et al.)", dropping "shown"; the meaning is unchanged. `figures.py --write` and `--render` were run and the claim quotes refreshed; Fetterman claim (1) was reworded to the new label and left unticked for the author.

Also closing an `open` item of `docs/lessons.md`: the rule "when you correct a claim, rewrite the whole sentence", learned on 2026-10-27, existed only in the log although the blog draft says the agent has it. It is now in Draft step 3 of `AGENTS.md`, together with re-reading the title, Highlights and Abstract after a correction; the lesson's status is `rule only`.

## [2026-11-23] lint | log archives moved to wiki/log-archive/

The seven archive files of the log sat in the root of `wiki/` beside the concept pages, where they crowded the Obsidian file list and showed up as root nodes in the graph view (grouping the root pages with `path:wiki` after `path:wiki/papers` caught them too). They are moved with `git mv` to `wiki/log-archive/`, unchanged except that their link back to the log is now `../log.md`; `log.md` stays in `wiki/`, where the LLM-wiki pattern, AGENTS.md and index.md expect it. `scripts/rotate_log.py` writes new archives to the folder and lists them in the header as `log-archive/<name>`; `scripts/check.py` reads the log headers, and the lesson evidence, from `log.md` and the folder. AGENTS.md, README.md and `docs/lessons.md` name the new place; to search the whole history, grep `wiki/log.md wiki/log-archive/`. Moved now, while there are seven archives rather than dozens.

## [2026-11-23] lint | first PDF export reviewed: caption breaks, Figure 1 contrast and empty pages fixed

The first PDF printed from `main-export.html` (33 pages) passed the text checks of `docs/pdf-export-notes.md`: no comments, no YAML, no stray asterisks, \#CM01 printed without its backslash, the Fridericia formula rendered, both tables within the margins, links underlined, no browser header or footer. Three layout faults were found by looking at every page. (1) The Figure 2 caption sat alone at the foot of page 16 and was split over two pages, apart from the figure: the flowchart is almost a page tall, so caption and figure could not fit together. (2) Both table captions were left at the foot of the page before their table; `print.css` bound captions to images but had no rule for tables. (3) In Figure 1 the 2022 and 2025 sections had white text on light purple, the default Mermaid timeline colours, which nearly vanish in print. Fixes: `docs/print.css` keeps a caption paragraph whole and with the following image or table, and limits an image to 200 mm high so its caption fits on the same page; `scripts/figures.py` sets black labels for all twelve timeline colour scales, and both figures were re-rendered. In addition, Highlights, Abbreviations, Acknowledgements and About the author no longer start a page of their own. A test print with headless Edge gave 30 pages with every caption beside its figure or table; the deposited PDF is still to be printed from the browser by the researcher.

## [2026-11-23] lint | Zenodo deposit: the PDF only, no HTML

Decided to deposit the PDF only, not the HTML as an additional file as planned since 2026-10-26. Zenodo accepts any file type and recommends none; for a preprint the PDF is the expected format, Zenodo previews it, and it can be cited by page. The HTML would add nothing that is not kept elsewhere: the repository snapshot planned for the same deposit (ToDo B2) archives `main.md`, the Mermaid sources of the figures and the wiki under a DOI of their own. It would also add work and a point of failure: it loads its two figures from `figures/` beside it, so they would have to be embedded before every deposit. Zenodo's handling of HTML, an open question in the plan, therefore no longer needs checking. The HTML remains the intermediate the PDF is printed from. `ToDo.md` (B2) and the deposit plan in `docs/pdf-export-notes.md` are updated.

## [2026-11-23] lint | published on Zenodo: preprint and repository snapshot

The paper is published as a preprint on Zenodo, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24459573 (version 1, 2026-11-23, CC BY 4.0, the PDF only, *References* Mäki 2023). The repository at publication, GitHub release `v1.0`, is a separate Software record, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24459822, uploaded as the release zip rather than through the GitHub integration (the researcher did not want to link the accounts); text CC BY 4.0, code in `scripts/` MIT. Two records rather than one, because they differ in type and licence and the preprint was to carry the PDF only. The snapshot's *Is supplement to* points to 10.5281/zenodo.24459572, the paper's concept DOI (all versions), which was checked to resolve to the paper. The paper was published before the snapshot existed, so its *Is supplemented by* link to the snapshot is still to be added by editing the record's metadata, which needs no new version. README now names both DOIs and says that the published text is the PDF, since `main.md` may change after `v1.0`.

## [2026-11-25] lint | AGENTS.md cut to the rules of every task; Ingest, Draft and Lint became skills

Outside feedback: AGENTS.md (166 lines but 25 kB, about 6,000 tokens) goes with every request, so a short question or a reading task carried the whole Ingest, Draft and claims-file procedure; skills and hooks need no declaration there, a description of how the repository works belongs in the README, and the Karpathy skill was about coding. AGENTS.md now holds only what applies to every task (layout, a table of procedures, never invent citations, `raw/` immutable, `notes.md`, escaped hashes, the Tag vocabulary, references, decisions in the log, the finishing checks, surgical changes), about 5.6 kB. The procedures moved to `.claude/skills/ingest`, `draft` (with `claims-file.md`, read only when the claims file is edited) and `lint`, which now also covers applying approved fixes. The Ingest checklist drawn from the log (`docs/ideas.md`) went into the ingest skill, with a definition of done for each skill. `skills/karpathy-guidelines` was removed: it sat outside `.claude/skills/`, so Claude Code never loaded it, and its content was already in the behavioural rules. Compatibility with agents other than Claude Code (the researcher's wish) is kept by the procedures table in AGENTS.md, which names the skill file to read for each task, and by the finishing-check rule, which tells an agent without the hook to run the scripts itself. `check.py` reads the Tag vocabulary from the new bullet; its messages now point to the skills. The README, `docs/ideas.md`, the grinding and grill-paper skills were updated to match.

Checks: a separate agent compared the old AGENTS.md rule by rule with the new files; the gaps it found were fixed (the reference-year and verbatim-copy rules moved to AGENTS.md, because a reference fix loads neither task skill; "or becomes central", "include the check.py output", "the authors' own page" and the ban on quoted or dropped hashes restored; the draft description covers edits of the claims file alone). Five headless `claude -p` runs in plan mode (no edits): an ingest question read the ingest skill and started with the verify-first pass; a draft request read the draft skill; a health check invoked the lint skill; a factual question used no skill; and with skills disabled (`--disable-slash-commands`, as a stand-in for an agent without skills) the ingest question still found the skill through the AGENTS.md table. A bogus tag was still reported by `check.py`. Not changed: the `.claude/settings.json` rule that denies edits to `notes.md` still contradicts "append a bullet only when asked", as before the split. Carried into `llm-wiki-academic-template` (local folder, not committed): its AGENTS.md went from 23.3 kB to 7.6 kB (the literature-search rule stays there), the three skills were written for its own `claim_quotes.py`, which finds sources from the claims-file headings, and its `check.py` passes with 0 errors and 0 warnings, the Tag vocabulary still read.

## [2026-11-25] lint | notes.md stays closed to the agent; the append clause removed

AGENTS.md said the agent may append a dated bullet to `notes.md` when asked, while `.claude/settings.json` has denied every edit of `notes.md` since 2026-11-11, so the clause could not be followed. The log shows no append by the agent, ever. The researcher's decision: keep the deny rule and remove the clause, here and in `llm-wiki-academic-template`; a thought to keep is written in the chat, dated and ready to paste, and the researcher adds it. Declined: changing the deny rule to ask (as for `raw/`), because that would weaken a hard limit for a feature never used, and an approval given by mistake would mix the agent's text into the researcher's own notes.
